name: Mem0
note: A decent drop-in memory layer if you don't want to build it yourself.
good: Handles entity extraction and temporal memory out of the box. Simple API.
bad: Black box retrieval. You can't tune the embedding weights easily if it returns the wrong context.
price: Free tier available. Usage based after.

name: Zep
note: Built specifically for chat history and agent memory.
good: Fast. Handles summarization of older context windows automatically.
bad: Self-hosting can be heavy. Their proprietary retrieval algorithms aren't always transparent.
price: Free (Open source) or cloud pricing starting around $20/mo.

name: Pinecone
note: The default vector database, but overkill for many.
good: Fully managed, scales instantly. Serverless offering is great for intermittent loads.
bad: Not a 'memory' solution, just a database. You have to write all the chunking, embedding, and retrieval logic.
price: Serverless is pay-per-read/write. Pods start at $70/mo.

name: Weaviate
note: My preferred vector DB if I need hybrid search.
good: BM25 + Vector search works beautifully out of the box. Good self-hosting.
bad: Cloud pricing can jump quickly. The API can feel over-engineered for simple tasks.
price: Open source free. Cloud starts around $25/mo.

name: Chroma
note: Best for local development and small apps.
good: Runs locally with zero setup. Integrates with everything.
bad: Distributed/cloud offering has been 'coming soon' forever. Not for large scale production.

name: Motorhead
bad: Development seems to have slowed down. Small community.

name: Qdrant
note: The rising star of vector databases. Rust-based and fast.
good: Incredible performance. Great filtering capabilities alongside vector search.
bad: Complex configuration options can be daunting for beginners.
price: Open source free. Cloud free tier is generous.

name: Postgres (pgvector)
note: What you should probably actually use if you already have a database.
good: You don't need a new database. Joins relational data with vectors effortlessly.
bad: Performance at extreme scale (100M+ vectors) requires tuning. Not a 'memory' API, just raw storage.
